Hoffmann sign, an upgoing plantar, spastic speech) and lower motor neuron damage (wasting,
fasciculations, low motor amplitudes, denervation on EMG) in the same regions, now spread across all
four: bulbar, cervical, thoracic and lumbosacral. Sensation is normal. The MRI excludes the structural
conditions that can mimic this, the bloods exclude the treatable ones, and the EMG shows the process
is active and widespread. He meets the Gold Coast criteria without ambiguity. In retrospect he probably
met them a year ago.

spinal cord. The muscle itself is healthy; it wastes because the nerve supply dies. Sensation, eye
movements, bladder and bowel are spared. Thinking is usually spared, though about half of patients
develop some change in word-finding or executive function, and Alex's reduced verbal fluency is of that
kind. The cause in his case, as in about nine of ten cases, is unknown.

have started today, and edaravone, which we will discuss. A third drug, tofersen, is the first treatment to
act on a cause of ALS. It is an antisense oligonucleotide that silences a faulty SOD1 gene, and because it
cannot cross the blood-brain barrier it is given by lumbar puncture every month. Health Canada
authorised it with conditions in February 2025. It applies to the roughly two per cent of patients who
carry a SOD1 mutation. Alex's genetic panel was negative, so, like most people with this disease, he has
no treatment directed at its cause. Beyond drugs, what has been shown to lengthen life is care at a
multidisciplinary clinic, keeping his weight up, and breathing support at night once it is needed.

favour. The pattern will continue: the right hand and leg will weaken further and the left side will follow;
speech, swallowing and breathing have begun to be involved and will progress. I have been honest with
them that the median survival from symptom onset is two to four years, that the range is wide, and that
the decisions ahead (a feeding tube, ventilation at night, how he wants to communicate when speech
is difficult) are better made early. I have referred him to the regional ALS clinic, which will see him every

import type { Patient } from './pipeline'

/**
 * Pull the structured patient profile out of a case file's text. Clinical
 * letters repeat facts as they change (age 45 → 47, FVC 78 → 76), so for
 * anything that evolves we take the LAST mention, which is the most recent.
 * Anything the file doesn't state is left as "Not stated", never guessed.
 */

const NOT_STATED = 'Not stated'
const PROVINCES = 'Ontario|Quebec|British Columbia|Alberta|Manitoba|Saskatchewan|Nova Scotia|New Brunswick|Newfoundland and Labrador|Prince Edward Island|ON|QC|BC|AB|MB|SK|NS|NB|NL|PE'

const last = (text: string, re: RegExp) => [...text.matchAll(re)].at(-1)
const sentence = (s: string) => s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1)

export function parseCasePatient(pages: string[]): Patient {
  const t = pages.join('\n').replace(/\s+/g, ' ')

  // "Alex Chen, 45, male" … "Alex Chen, 47": the name and the latest age.
  const people = [...t.matchAll(/\b([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+), (\d{1,3})\b(?:,? (male|female))?/g)]
  const name = people[0]?.[1] ?? 'Uploaded patient'
  const mentions = people.filter((m) => m[1] === name)
  const age = Number(mentions.at(-1)?.[2] ?? NaN)
  const sexWord = mentions.find((m) => m[3])?.[3]
  const sex = sexWord === 'male' ? 'M' : sexWord === 'female' ? 'F' : ''

  const onset = t.match(/\b(limb|bulbar|spinal|respiratory)[ -]onset\b/i)?.[1]
  const weeks = last(t, /(\d+) weeks? (?:from|since) diagnosis/gi)?.[1]
  const months = last(t, /(\d+) months? (?:from|since) diagnosis/gi)?.[1]
  const alsfrs = last(t, /ALSFRS-R:? (\d{1,2}) ?(?:of|\/) ?48/g)?.[1]
  const slope = t.match(/decline of (?:about )?([\d.]+) points? (?:per|a) month/i)?.[1]
  // Digits can't be skipped between "vital capacity" and the value, so a table title can't borrow a later number.
  const fvc = last(t, /vital capacity[^.\d]{0,40}(\d{2,3})(?: and \d{2,3})? per ?cent/gi)?.[1]

  const panel = t.match(/Genetic panel:? (.+?) (No pathogenic variant detected|Pathogenic variant detected[^.]*)/i)
  const genes = panel?.[1].replace(/ repeat expansion/g, '').replace(/ and (\d+) further genes/, ' + $1 more')
  const genetics = panel ? (/^no/i.test(panel[2]) ? `Panel negative (${genes})` : `${panel[2]} (${genes})`) : NOT_STATED

  const med = t.match(/Medication:? ([A-Z][^.]+?)(?: since [^.]*)?\./)?.[1]
  const medications = med ? [med] : /takes no medication/i.test(t) ? ['None'] : [NOT_STATED]

  const place = t.match(new RegExp(`\\b([A-Z][a-z]+), (${PROVINCES})\\b`))
  // What the patient has turned down or is hoping for, in the file's own words.
  const preferences = [...t.matchAll(/[^.]*\b(?:declined|[Ww]ants to|[Ww]ould like to)\b[^.]*\./g)]
    .map((m) => sentence(m[0].trim().replace(/^(?:He|She|They) (?:has |have )?/, '').replace(/\.$/, '')))
    .filter((s) => s.length <= 90)
    .slice(0, 4)

  return {
    id: name.split(' ').map((w) => w[0]).join(''),
    label: name,
    age,
    sex,
    onset: onset ? `${sentence(onset.toLowerCase())} onset` : 'Onset not stated',
    monthsSinceDx: weeks ? Math.round(Number(weeks) / 4.345) : Number(months ?? NaN),
    alsfrs: Number(alsfrs ?? NaN),
    slope: slope ? -Number(slope) : NaN,
    fvc: Number(fvc ?? NaN),
    genetics,
    medications,
    comorbidities: /no significant past history/i.test(t) ? [] : [NOT_STATED],
    location: place ? `${place[1]}, ${place[2]}` : NOT_STATED,
    coverage: NOT_STATED,
    preferences,
    fusEligible: false,
  }
}

I've rebuilt Patient monitoring: you now pick a patient from cards first, then see their profile laid out like shadcn's dashboard example. The frontend type-checks, but I haven't seen it on screen, because my browser tool still can't open the dev server.

**Step 1: choose a patient**
- There is one card per patient, showing initials, name, "47M · limb-onset ALS", ALSFRS-R 32/48, FVC 76%, the last visit date and a "2 flags" badge.
- Only Alex Chen has monitoring data over time, so his is the only real card. I didn't make up other patients. Next to it is a dashed **Add a patient** card that goes to the case upload page.
- The chosen patient is kept in the address (`/home/patient?p=alex-chen`), so the browser's back button and the "← All patients" button both return to the list.

**Step 2: the patient's profile**
- **Four stat cards**, each with a big number, a trend badge and two short lines underneath:
  - ALSFRS-R 32/48, down 0.6 a month
  - Sitting vital capacity 76%, 61% lying flat
  - Weight 77.5 kg, down 10%
  - Neurofilament light 88 pg/mL, 5.9× the reference
- **One trend chart** with a switch between ALSFRS-R, vital capacity and weight. This replaces three separate charts.
- **Side by side:** "ALSFRS-R by domain" as plain bars, and "What to watch" listing the case file's concerns. Each concern has a warning or eye icon, so the level doesn't depend on colour alone.
- **One measurements table** holding speech, hand strength and all the lab and clinic tests. Each row has a status badge with an icon. This replaces the speech meters, hand meters and the collapsible tests table.
- The divider lines are gone: no grey footer strip or line under each card, no lines between flags, and no dashed chart grid.

**What I cut to reduce clutter:**
- **The strength table and the road-to-diagnosis timeline.** The timeline tells the "waited two years for a diagnosis" story, so say if you want it back in a simpler form.
- **The dashed carpal-tunnel and diagnosis markers on the chart.**

The changes are in `src/components/overview-dashboard.tsx`, plus a one-line change in `src/pages/Home.tsx`. Nothing is committed.

**About your earlier question on tabs not opening:** your new message interrupted me before I'd finished checking. What I did confirm is that my changes didn't remove any of those tabs from the sidebar or the page routing. But the working tree has edits I didn't make: `fus-page.tsx`, `page-header.tsx` and `alex-case.ts` are new, and `sample-data.ts` has been deleted. Those are the likely place to look.
